I've had probably the worst semester of my life. She made it a lot better. So accommodating and kind. Funny too. She's just a great person, but also a great prof. You get participation grades for going to class most days so it is important to go but the class is enjoyable. She will also allow you to redo papers and extra time if you just ask.

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, this class was really frustrating. Professor never explained things in a way that actually helped, and whenever students asked for clarification, it often felt like we were being talked down to. Instead of feeling supported. It made the whole course stressful and discouraging, and it didn't feel like we were set up to learn or succeed.

While Ghosh is a kind and respectable professor, this course was not structured very well. There were only two homework assignments and two exams. We also did not go deep enough into proving algorithms and were not required to know how to do that for the exam. If you did poorly once, there was little opportunity to fix it. Minimal partial credit.

This class was a constant battle between the students and the instructor just to get him to follow standard academic procedures. He tried to schedule presentations during Thanksgiving and dead week, and graded our assignments and exams nonsensically. He only moved the presentations and added a curve after the department caught wind of his neglect.

Dr. Ghosh seems to care deeply about the success of his students, but his traditional format of lectures and exams is weak. Not all of the issues with CS 470 are Dr. Ghosh's fault - students are, by and large, unprepared for the class. This is essentially an unsolvable problem, but Dr. Ghosh could try to include more homework and smaller quizzes.

Ghosh is not receptive to student feedback. I and other students voiced several different concerns with the course, and did not achieve any change. Ghosh vaguely blamed the department for the course structure and didnt take accountability. The lack of assignments and high stakes few question exams were entirely his fault. I hope he works on this

He's very knowledgable about game theory but seems too smart to understand how to teach students the basics of the material. In-person tests were relatively easy. When class switched to online due to COVID-19, he assigned book chapters and problems and posted three five minute videos, became self-taught...I had to switch to P/F to protect my GPA...

Only grades are 4 tests (1 drop). Attendance is not required although if you go to almost every class I guarantee you will get at least a B and an A if you really like Economics. Posts problem sets on his website which are similar to ones on tests. The MC is a little challenging though so you must read the book, regardless. Great class/teacher!

Dr. Peterson is the man. Will always work with you on deadlines as long as you come to class and participate. Keeps lectures fun and engaging and you end up being friends with your classmates after this course due to the amount of socratic seminars/debates. Would recommend anyone to take this course.

There are a lot of weekly readings and a weekly 3-question quiz that is kind of confusing, but the TA will likely clarify a question if you are confused. Tests are difficult but graded leniently.
